A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Knee-Deep in C-RASP: A Transformer Depth Hierarchy. All pages, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison. The original appendices are retained, with a new positional-encoding appendix inserted before the notation index.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original transformer training and evaluation on synthetic languages L3–L12, with accuracy results in Figures 2 and 4.

after.justification: Section 5 reports original transformer experiments on L3–L12 under revised training and evaluation settings, with results in Figures 2 and 4.

M1.justification: Appendix F expands the formal transformer models beyond v1's model without positional encodings, adding sinusoidal input embeddings, RoPE query/key rotations and ALiBi attention biases. Appendix B.1 also adds averaging when the attention denominator is zero. These are changes to the modeled procedures; the empirical transformers still omit positional encodings.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same L3–L12 next-token prediction tasks, but sampled sequence lengths shift from 101–300 to 201–400, replacing shorter input conditions with longer ones. The new Dyck examples and neutral-letter languages are explanatory or theoretical, not additional empirical datasets.

E2.justification: Both empirical comparisons contain transformers with depths 1–10 and no positional encodings. No external baseline is added or removed. The newly discussed positional-encoding variants are not evaluated as comparators.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 moves training/validation from lengths 101–150 to 201–250. Strings per bin decrease from 2,000 to 1,000, with training/validation counts changing from 1,600/400 to 800/200. Width choices change from 64/256 to 256/512, learning rates from 10^-5/10^-6 to 10^-4/10^-5, and the budget from 10 to 25 epochs. V2 describes multiclass classification where v1 specifies a sigmoid. Adam and exact-sequence accuracy are retained.

E4.justification: The existing depth-sensitivity and length-generalization analysis is revised to use longer training and test sequences, changing the evidence about robustness beyond training lengths. The questions investigated remain the same; no separate component ablations or positional-encoding experiments are added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the accuracy results. V2's compute averages do not introduce experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 2 and 4 contain replacement accuracy grids under the revised protocol. For example, v1 reports 16% for depth-10 L12 at lengths 101–150; v2 reports 86% at 201–250 and 62% at 351–400. V1's discussion of widespread failure for k ≥ 10 is removed. These are protocol-specific replacement findings, not controlled same-setting gains.

T1.justification: New Appendix F defines the Y and MOD extensions, develops normalization and padding constructions, introduces neutral-letter languages E_k, and states depth hierarchies and simulations for positional-encoding variants. Sinusoidal and RoPE results assume periodic angles that are rational multiples of pi. Separately, Lemma D.1 changes its future-count rewrite to use strict past counting.

C1.justification: The abstract now claims a depth hierarchy for transformers with positional encodings, including RoPE and ALiBi. V1 treated positional encodings as future theoretical work. The original claims about C-RASP equivalence, the hierarchy without positional encodings and its empirical predictive relevance remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds a tentative implication for phoneme n-gram recognition and explains that positional-encoding experiments were omitted because the negative results may require extremely long inputs. It removes the discussion distinguishing expressibility from learnability after high-k failures and adds data diversity as a possible practical factor.

D1.justification: V2 revises the documented experimental hyperparameters and adds resource information: an internal GPU cluster, average compute of 9.37 × 10^4 TFLOPs and 936.8 MiB memory for the described training loop. The experimental code link is retained, while the disclosure of LLM assistance is revised.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Press et al. on ALiBi, Su et al. on RoFormer and Mesnard et al. on Gemma, and connects the extended logic to C-RASP[local,periodic]. The principal positioning against earlier depth-separation work remains. Chen et al.'s 2024-to-2025 update refers to the same work.

P1.justification: V2 adds a Dyck-language walkthrough, refines the reduction intuition, repeats theorem statements beside appendix proofs and integrates Appendix F. The main narrative and section ordering are largely retained. Cross-references, acknowledgements and conference information are also updated.

P2.justification: V2 adds two Dyck trace tables and Figure 5 illustrating the padding construction. Figure 4 retains its four-panel heatmap format but changes length labels and its caption; Figure 2 now reproduces the longest-length panel. Existing theoretical diagrams are retained, with modest page reflow.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful worked examples, compute disclosure and a potentially substantial theoretical extension. However, new Lemma F.1 rewrites Y(not Q_a) as not(Y Q_a): at the first position these are respectively false and true under Eq. (20a). This leaves a proof step used by the subsequent extension incorrect as written. The replacement experiments also change several settings together. The documented benefits and unresolved theoretical support prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
